title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
authors: Guillermo Arias-Tamargo, Philip Boyle Smith, Rishi Mouland, Max Velásquez Cotini Hutt
abstract: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.
summary: This paper develops a general framework to study how continuous symmetries are preserved when quantum field theories are placed on a boundary. By using Chern-Simons theory, the authors construct topological defects whose properties, such as the resulting 'twist lines,' are analyzed using advanced algebraic structures. This work is crucial for understanding symmetry protection in strongly correlated and topological matter systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical problem of defining boundary conditions for quantum field theories (QFTs) on manifolds with boundaries while preserving continuous symmetries without anomalies.
main_result: The authors provide a general construction for topological defects preserving symmetries using Chern-Simons theory, showing that the resulting twist lines can be intrinsically non-invertible for non-abelian symmetries.
method: The methodology involves analyzing Dirac fermions via a 3D Chern-Simons formulation, utilizing concepts from topological quantum field theory (TQFT), and employing algebraic tools like bimodule categories to characterize the defects.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 2D Dirac fermions and Weyl fermions, relating the boundary physics to topological defects (analogous to 't Hooft lines) in chiral gauge theories, with specific examples including the 3450 model and $SU(2) 	imes SU(4) 	imes U(1)^2$ symmetries.
key_observables: Twist lines, boundary central charge, and the $	ext{mod-}2$ valued SPT class of the folded boundary state.
important_parameters: The symmetry group $G$, the number of fermions $N$, and the relationship between the rank of $G$ and $N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the bottom boundaries are topological and uses advanced mathematical machinery involving super-modular tensor categories.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the hierarchy of difficulties for symmetries (equal-rank vs. conformally-embedded). Figure 2 shows the TQFT construction of the defect, and Figure 3 illustrates the process of twisted scattering.
paper_structure: The paper builds from a general framework using Chern-Simons theory to construct defects, details the mathematical machinery using bimodule categories to characterize the defects, and applies this to specific abelian and non-abelian symmetry examples.
why_interesting: The deep connection between topological defects, symmetry protection, and non-invertible symmetries provides powerful theoretical tools for understanding boundary physics in condensed matter systems, particularly those exhibiting topological order.
